newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plate Glass says yr shr may not match 95/96.
newsitem.headline: Plate Glass says yr shr may not match 95/96.

text.p: South Africa's Plate Glass & Shatterprufe Industries Ltd (PGSI) said on Friday its full year results will have difficulty matching those achieved in the previous financial year unless the economy improved markedly.

"Without... a marked recovery in the South African economy, and in particular the markets served by the group, PGSI will have difficulty matching the results achieved in the second half of last year and therefore the year as a whole," chairman Ronnie Lubner said in a statement.
Results for the six months to end-September, released on Friday, show earnings falling almost five percent to 316.4 cents a share. The dividend was held steady at 149.0 cents.
Lubner blamed the fall in earnings on the depressed state of the glass and board markets in southern Africa.

Although he expected increased efficiencies from group operations in the second half of the year, this might not be enough, he said. "(No) amount of production efficiency can substitute for a market that is just not there," Lubner said.
He remained confident that offshore operations would continue to perform well, providing the company with a hedge against local market conditions and the rand's depreciation.
